To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of views required for high-resolution micro-computed tomography can be reduced to 25% of the typically acquired views, and that the reconstruction accuracy is comparable to filtered back projection, if measurement noise is not very high.

(a) the use of compressed sensing based iterative reconstruction techniques in high-resolution micro CT can significantly reduce the scan time and (b) a 3D phantom for micro-CT is proposed and used for analyzing the reconstruction accuracy of the proposed techniques.
the number of views in high-resolution microCT can be reduced to 8th of the typically acquired views, while maintaining accuracy, using compressed-sensing-based iterative techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new algorithms and techniques for high-resolution micro-computed tomography.
improving the quality of 3D imaging in high-resolution micro-computed tomography (micro-CT).
developing new reconstruction techniques and algorithms to enable high-resolution imaging in micro-CT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of advanced reconstruction techniques is highly recommended in high-resolution micro-computed tomography (CT).
the use of iterative techniques for reconstruction in high-resolution micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is a promising approach to reduce the scan time.
the use of iterative reconstruction methods for few view micro-CT imaging is feasible and can be used for high-resolution micro CT imaging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the reconstruction accuracy of few-view reconstruction can be improved significantly by the proposed 3D phantom and iterative reconstruction techniques, while maintaining the scan time at a reasonable level.
the number of views in micro-CT may be reduced to one eighth without significant loss in image quality.

, in the case of micro-CT, we can reduce the number of views by an order of magnitude without any loss in reconstruction accuracy, and this is achieved by the use of iterative techniques that are based on compressed-sensing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for high-resolution micro CT, a few view reconstruction can be performed with a high degree of accuracy.
, if measurement noise is not too high, then the number of views in micro-CT may be reduced to as low as 1/8th of the typically acquired number of views without sacrificing accuracy.
the reconstruction quality is much more sensitive to measurement noise than to the number of views.
